name: ddl_no_exclusive_lock_lq1686_20261109
comment: ANCHOR: LQ-20261107-1686 - runtime DDL must not take a lock to assert what is already true.
Five writers asserted their schema on every call: ensure_schema() (llm_consumption_log,
IF NOT EXISTS suppresses the error, not the lock: an ADD COLUMN asks for ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the
table whether or not the column exists, and the CREATEs resolved a name they then did not need.
2026-11-09 14:18-15:19 ET: 124 lock timeouts, 5 deadlocks against a 3 s lock_timeout.
All five now ask the catalog first (lib.ddl_guard.relation_exists / column_exists, or an
information_schema read where the module already had one; no table lock) and issue DDL only for
what is genuinely absent. The schema itself moved to
The tests drive the real functions against a fake cursor that answers catalog reads the way
PostgreSQL would and records every statement: a deployed schema must execute no DDL, and a
genuinely missing column or table must still be created (a guard that skips everything is worse
than the lock). Fake IO: no database, no broker.
